title: Choose the Cathode Gauze composition
question: Which layout should become the visual contract for every Last Train surface?

options.label: Cathode Stack
options.lineage: all departures held as ghost numerals behind one struck answer
options.thesis: The final train occupies the whole first impression while earlier services remain visible as decaying context.
options.viewport: A monumental central 23:47 sits above a quiet vertical service list and terminal first-back line.
options.risk: The destination transition is clear, but the list below is the most conventional of the three compositions.

options.label: Route Strike
options.lineage: a chronological rail with active and ghosted time states
options.thesis: A single vertical strike line makes the service sequence physical while the last departure snaps forward at monumental scale.
options.viewport: Station and direction live in a persistent edge index; 23:47 commands the upper-right and earlier trains descend along one illuminated rail.
options.risk: Its asymmetry is memorable but needs careful Dynamic Type adaptation so the left edge never competes with the times.

options.label: Island Relay
options.lineage: the selected departure relayed between the app and Dynamic Island
options.thesis: The Dynamic Island becomes the origin of the interface, with the chosen train traveling visibly between the phone and the live countdown.
options.viewport: A beam drops from the Island into the central 23:47, earlier departures compress into a fixed chronology strip, and first back closes the screen.
options.risk: It expresses the new Live Activity connection best, but the Island cannot become essential navigation on devices without one.
